fact_check_verdict: Publish as a statement of what three documents say and don't. AIDEA bought shares in a reactor startup. The AI wording is NuCube's market boilerplate. AIDEA's own release lists data centers, never AI. No size, site, price or date for NuCube in Alaska.

claims.spoken: On October nineteenth, an Idaho company called NuCube Energy announced a twenty five million dollar investment from Alaska.
requires: Press release dated October 19th inside the SEC Form 425. Say announced, never signed.

claims.spoken: The money comes from AIDEA, the state's development authority.
claims.on_screen: AIDEA · ALASKA INDUSTRIAL DEVELOPMENT AND EXPORT AUTHORITY
requires: AIDEA is a state-backed investment authority. Attribute the purchase to AIDEA's release and NuCube's SEC filing.

claims.spoken: NuCube builds a small nuclear reactor called NuSun.
requires: Exact wording: solid-state, heat-pipe-cooled reactor. Never state a size, price, site or date for NuSun.

claims.spoken: AIDEA agreed to buy twenty five million dollars of NuCube shares at nine dollars and twenty five cents each.
requires: Class A ordinary shares. Attributed to the SEC Form 425.

claims.spoken: That is about fourteen and a half percent below the reference price of ten eighty two.
requires: Say reference price, the filing's term for the price used to set the exchange ratio.

claims.spoken: NuCube is in the middle of a merger with a company called Launch Two.
requires: Say proposed or in the middle of, never completed.

claims.spoken: That merger needs seventy five million dollars in cash to close, and AIDEA's money counts toward it.
requires: The filing's Minimum Cash Condition.

claims.spoken: AIDEA also gets half a warrant per share, to buy more at eleven fifty within five years.
claims.on_screen: HALF A WARRANT A SHARE · $11.50 · 5 YEARS
requires: Exact wording: one-half of one warrant per share exercisable at $11.50 within 5 years.

claims.spoken: NuCube's chief executive called AIDEA the anchor investor.
requires: Quote: "As our anchor investor, AIDEA gives us a solid capital foundation". Anchor investor in the company's current financing. Attribute to Rabiti and the SEC filing.

claims.spoken: The governor said Alaska has always been a place where innovation is driven by necessity.
claims.on_screen: "INNOVATION IS DRIVEN BY NECESSITY" · GOV. DUNLEAVY
requires: Verbatim: "Alaska has always been a place where innovation is driven by necessity." From AIDEA's release and the SEC filing, never Alaska Business.

claims.spoken: AIDEA's deputy director said affordable energy is about more than a utility bill.
claims.on_screen: "MORE THAN A UTILITY BILL" · BRANDON BREFCZYNSKI, AIDEA
requires: Verbatim: "Affordable energy is about more than a utility bill." Source is AIDEA's release and Alaska Business, never the SEC filing. Title: Deputy Director.

claims.spoken: NuCube's own filing says the word AI once, in a list of market trends.
claims.on_screen: NUCUBE'S FILING · "AI DATA CENTER ENERGY DEMAND" · ONCE
requires: The phrase sits in the forward-looking statements, a general market sentence, not Alaska-specific text. Say NuCube's own filing. 'AI' appears nowhere else in the filing.

claims.spoken: The paragraphs about Alaska never mention AI.
requires: Checked against the SEC Form 425 quotes, headline and AIDEA paragraphs, and Alaska Business. Say the paragraphs about Alaska in the filing. Do not say no Alaska document anywhere.

claims.spoken: AIDEA's own release does list data centers, next to mining, seafood and manufacturing, as places cheaper energy could help.
claims.on_screen: AIDEA · MINING · SEAFOOD · MANUFACTURING · DATA CENTERS
requires: A list item. The release never says AI. Do not say AIDEA bought it for data centers.

claims.spoken: None of the three documents gives a size, a site, a price or a date for a NuCube reactor in Alaska.
claims.on_screen: SIZE · SITE · PRICE · DATE · NOT STATED
requires: Three documents read in full or by extraction: SEC Form 425, AIDEA release 19-2026, Alaska Business. Say in the three documents we read.

claims.spoken: AIDEA's release says the benefits depend on technology development, regulatory approvals, financing and host communities.
claims.on_screen: DEPENDS ON · TECHNOLOGY · APPROVALS · FINANCING · HOST COMMUNITIES
requires: Paraphrase of the AIDEA caveat: depend on successful technology development, regulatory approvals, project financing, and work with prospective host communities.

claims.spoken: The release also says NuCube is committed to deploying its reactor in Alaska.
claims.on_screen: NUCUBE · COMMITTED TO DEPLOYMENT IN ALASKA · NO DATE
requires: Attribute to AIDEA's release: NuCube is also committed to advancing the commercial deployment of its microreactor technology in Alaska. Open-ended, no number or date.

claims.spoken: The one reactor already planned for Alaska belongs to a different company, Oklo, at Eielson Air Force Base.
requires: Oklo's project page. Say Oklo plans, never operating.

claims.spoken: Oklo says it should make at least five megawatts of electricity, in the early twenty thirties.
requires: Oklo's words: at least 5 MWe, target operations early 2030s following NRC licensing and other federal approvals. Never say 2030. Never say paused.

claims.spoken: Oklo says drilling to check the ground begins late this year.
requires: Oklo's page: borehole drilling and ground investigations to begin late 2026.

claims.spoken: Meanwhile Enstar's president says this winter's gas shortage is eighteen days, or three billion cubic feet.
claims.on_screen: ENSTAR'S PRESIDENT · WINTER GAS SHORTAGE · 18 DAYS · 3 BCF
requires: Attribute to Enstar president John Sims via Anchorage Daily News, September 16th. Not a state figure.

claims.spoken: NuCube was one of four companies the Energy Department picked for its Nuclear Energy Launch Pad on April twenty seventh.
requires: From AIDEA release 19-2026. Say according to AIDEA.

claims.spoken: The CEO said Alaska shows why dependable energy matters where traditional power is limited.
claims.on_screen: "WHERE ACCESS TO TRADITIONAL POWER IS LIMITED" · RABITI
requires: Rabiti in the SEC filing: Alaska illustrates the need for dependable energy where access to traditional power infrastructure can be limited.

do_not_say: that AIDEA invested for AI or data centers
that NuCube will build anything in Alaska by a date
that Oklo's Eielson project is paused (not found in 2026)
5 MW as the reactor size (it is at least 5 MWe, about 60 MWth)
that USNC went bankrupt or its patents moved (single secondary source, unverified)
founded 2023 (co-founded by Rabiti in 2023 per Alaska Business only)
that Alaska is the first state to invest
anything about Copper Valley Valdez as a current plan
